bull_bear.body: Cash and equivalents rose to **₹3,611 cr** (from ₹3,414 cr at FY26-end) despite ₹451 cr of capitalisation and a large working-capital build — the balance sheet remains net cash with no debt raised or discussed. The striking allocation choice this quarter is **working capital**: inventory ₹4,413 cr plus receivables ₹3,056 cr = **₹7,469 cr** deployed, with inventory alone at ~1.4× a quarter's revenue. That is a conscious trade — Nilima described abandoning a long-standing just-in-time philosophy: "The organization always went towards procuring material just in time and making sure there is no overstocking of material. But in the last few months, we decided we would go for a 3-month rolling inventory stocking." Capex continues on the three dedicated projects and peptide capacity. **No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary of any kind on this call.** On CSR, programmes reached **more than 1.8 million beneficiaries** across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Solvent price volatility is outside management's control and they said so.** "We see a few weeks of flat trend and then again, suddenly, we see a rise in — it all depends on the situation that's happening in the Middle East… it is not something in our hands, because it comes in bulk and affects the entire country the same way."
- **Inventory carries a two-sided risk.** If the Middle East de-escalates, Nilima conceded the reversal directly: "The cost would go down and the inventory — cost of inventory itself will go down… Would our volumes go down? Yes, they would because we wouldn't be stocking so much as well." A peace outcome is a *margin* event for Divi's, not just a cost relief. She refused to model FY27 inventory change: "It's a very difficult question to answer."
- **Freight and logistics remain degraded.** Elevated ocean *and* air rates; container and ISO-tank availability requiring active management; "congestion at several ports, tighter vessel allocation, cargo rollover, blank sailing and extended transit times."
- **Regulatory timing gates ₹2,000 cr of assets.** Every commercial start depends on the innovator's filing and the agency's review, and Divi's has no visibility. Assets are capitalised and depreciating now; revenue is not.
- **Kakinada's 1–2 year approval lag** means Unit 3 contributes only indirectly for the medium term.
- **Disclosure opacity.** Order book value, quantities, capacity, phase-wise pipeline split, product names, unit-wise utilisation, top-five product growth and the solvent-led price-change quantum were *all* refused under CDA. Investors cannot independently size the CS ramp.
- **INR dependence.** 10% constant-currency vs ~23% reported standalone growth means an INR reversal removes most of the growth optics. The forex line itself already swung ₹46 cr adverse YoY.
- **Utilisation at 80–85%** across all three units leaves thin absorption capacity if approvals arrive together.
- **Generic pricing has not structurally recovered** — see §12. The apparent API export price inflection is cost pass-through, not demand.
- **CDMO competition.** Asked directly whether the wave of Indian entrants and CDMO consolidation would bring margin pressure or harder customer negotiation, Kiran answered on reputation and EHS rather than pricing — and gave no assurance on pricing itself.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident on delivery, near-total on disclosure discipline. The CDA wall was invoked at least six separate times, and Kiran was candid that it was a constraint and not a dodge: "I wish to share more, but I'm bound by CDAs not to share." He also refused, consistently and on principle, to be drawn on competitors — "I cannot talk about other manufacturers, right? It's not right"; "I do not want to comment about why I'm different than others" — redirecting each time to what Divi's does rather than what rivals cannot.

Two credibility markers stand out. First, **Kiran corrected the record on Gadolinium unprompted** rather than letting a favourable prior-quarter reading stand: "That's what I said last time. I didn't say that we did validations." Volunteering a downgrade is a good sign. Second, **Nilima did not defend the Q1 margin print** — she pre-emptively guided the full year back to ~60% gross and flat EBITDA, and when IIFL laid out adjusted maths implying 55–58% gross / 28–30% EBITDA she added mechanism rather than contesting the arithmetic. That is closer to acknowledgement than rebuttal.

The one firm, checkable commitment is the repeated "double-digit growth no matter what" — restated three times by two speakers, and notably *not* raised despite a 24% Q1. Refusing to upgrade guidance off a flattered quarter is itself a discipline signal. Weaknesses: repeated audio problems forced multiple "can you repeat the question," the moderator cut off the first analyst mid-follow-up, and the CFO (Pasumarthy) was introduced but did not speak — all financial answers came from Nilima.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The growth is two-thirds currency.** Constant-currency standalone revenue grew **10%**; reported standalone grew ~23%. Divi's is ~90% export so the rupees are real, but the *rate* is not repeatable — and the FY27 guidance of "double-digit" is, on this reading, simply a restatement of the underlying 10% with the FX stripped out. The company has effectively told you the headline is not the number to model.
- **Nilima's ~60% full-year gross-margin guide is a confession about Q1.** Guiding the year to ~60% and EBITDA to "similar as last year" while printing ~68% gross means management expects roughly 800bps of the current gross margin to unwind. That is a bigger admission than the inventory debate — and it aligns almost exactly with IIFL's independently derived 55–58% adjusted figure.
- **Peace in the Middle East would hurt near-term reported margins.** The consensus read is that de-escalation relieves Divi's. Nilima said the opposite mechanically: cheaper solvents mean lower inventory *carrying values* and a smaller inventory build, which removes the very tailwind flattering Q1's gross margin. The cost relief is real but arrives with a destocking drag.
- **Validation-batch revenue is already flowing, contradicting the "dedicated capex contributes nothing yet" framing.** Kunal Dhamesha opened by asking management to confirm the CS uptick contained no dedicated-project contribution. Kiran declined to confirm: "a certain amount of product has also been shipped to the customer." So part of the mix shift to 60% CS is validation revenue — which is real, but non-recurring per project and not the commercial ramp.
- **Kakinada's return is a capacity arbitrage, not a revenue line — and the arbitrage is running while depreciation accrues.** Unit 3 earns by displacing pre-chemistry out of Units 1/2 and freeing regulator-approved GMP space for higher-value finished API. Any model that waits for "Unit 3 revenue" will mis-read the asset for the 1–2 years FDA takes to qualify the site.
- **Kiran demolished the sector-wide "generic pricing has bottomed" thesis — an important read-through beyond Divi's.** Goldman's analyst cited June API export data showing 7–8% positive price inflection. Kiran: "whatever you're seeing right now is a **market correction based on the raw material prices** that have taken a substantial hit. **It's not based on the markets have corrected and the pricing pressure has gone down.**" Apparent API pricing recovery across the Indian sector this quarter is cost pass-through — a revenue-line optic with no gross-profit content.
- **The moat argument was deliberately re-defined from scale to integration.** Asked twice whether Divi's aspires to match the largest global peptide player, Kiran refused the comparison and re-anchored on **"the largest *integrated* player"** — own resins, own FMOC/BOC protected amino acids, own tags. That is a company choosing a race it can win over one it cannot, and it is a more durable claim than capacity.
- **"We do not compete with our customers" is now doing heavy lifting.** As Indian formulation companies pivot into CDMO, Divi's absence of a formulations business becomes an active selling point rather than a strategic gap — the structural argument for why innovators keep choosing it as entrants multiply.
- **Solvent intensity in peptides is extreme and under-appreciated.** ~**2,000 litres of solvent per 1 kg** of peptide. A solvent price that doubles or triples is therefore a far larger threat to the peptide growth engine than to the small-molecule generic book — precisely the segment carrying the growth story.
- **Utilisation at 80–85% across all three units is the quiet constraint.** If the three dedicated projects, the iodine contracts and the 3–6-month generic launches all convert on schedule, there is not much slack. The 3,000-litre SPPS additions and Kakinada qualification are not optional expansion — they are the prerequisite for the FY28 story.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- World's largest API manufacturer in 10 of the 30 generic APIs it produces, with a presence in over 100 countries
- Trusted partner to 12 of the top 20 global pharmaceutical companies
- Backward integration deepened by Unit 3 at Kakinada, enabling in-house starting materials and intermediates with better supply assurance, cost efficiency and impurity control
- R&D depth via the Divi's Research Center and Process Development & Support Centres that handle scale-up from gram to commercial scale, impurity profiling, validation and technology transfer
- Regulatory track record: facilities at Hyderabad and Visakhapatnam repeatedly inspected by USFDA, EU GMP, Health Canada, TGA, ANVISA, COFEPRIS, PMDA and MFDS, with triple ISO certification
- Diversified therapeutic portfolio across cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer and central nervous system segments
- Wholly-owned marketing subsidiaries in the USA and Europe that bring the nutraceutical business closer to international customers
- Enterprise-wide risk management aggregated at corporate level under the Risk Management and Sustainability Committee, with a structured internal audit function reporting directly to the Audit Committee
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Occupational health and safety in chemical manufacturing — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: in pharmaceutical manufacturing, health and safety management systems must ensure uninterrupted and safe operations; incidents can have negative financial implications. Mitigated through systems aligned to the Factories Act, Explosives Act and ISO standards, with periodic audits and corrective/preventive action after incident reviews.
- Environment management — The Company's operations, if not managed properly, may result in risk to the environment, with negative financial implications. Managed through established environment management practices, risk assessments, periodic reviews and ISO 14001 certification.
- Waste management — Manufacturing requires abundant quantities of raw materials and proper management of waste generated; waste management risks may result in negative financial implications. Mitigated via recycle-and-reuse programmes, solvent recovery and reuse, green chemistry, and handling of solid waste per MoEFCC and Pollution Control Board conditions.
- Climate change and greenhouse gas emissions — Increased GHG emission levels may pose harmful effects to the environment and human health with negative financial implications. Mitigated by reducing dependency on fossil fuels, shifting to renewable sources for power and heat, SBTi-approved near-term and net-zero targets, and annual external verification of the GHG footprint per ISO 14064-1.
- Water management — Identified in the BRSR as a material responsible-business-conduct risk (water footprint, consumption, intensity and discharge are BRSR-Core assured attributes); the detail of the disclosure is truncated in the routed text.
- Geopolitical uncertainty, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruption — Global trade architecture is shifting from integrated globalisation toward fragmented networks driven by geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions and regulatory divergence, pushing procurement toward risk-adjusted frameworks, supplier diversification and inventory buffering. The Board notes FY 2025-26 was marked by a challenging global environment with evolving geopolitical and trade dynamics.
- Rising regulatory and compliance intensity — Escalating expectations for GMP, batch-to-batch consistency, data integrity and environmental and safety norms are raising both capital and operating intensity; compliance credibility becomes a key differentiator influencing supplier selection and contract longevity.
- Pricing and reimbursement pressure in developed markets — Pricing and reimbursement pressures across developed markets are intensifying scrutiny on value delivery and utilisation, and growth is becoming highly selective, concentrating in therapies with differentiated clinical outcomes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Generics (40% of standalone revenue; was 45%).** Volumes stable, pricing "continues to reflect competitive market conditions across products and geographies." Resilience credited to in-house manufacture of key starting materials and intermediates. Backing out nutraceuticals, an analyst computed generics at only single-digit-to-flat growth — not contested. Portfolio is ~**60 products**. New entries via post-patent-expiry filings: **4 DMFs**, Brivaracetam and Ticagrelor named, qualification underway, commercial volumes 3–6 months out, one long-term exclusivity in negotiation.
- **Custom Synthesis / CDMO (60% of standalone revenue; was 55%).** The quarter's swing factor. Projects run across "multiple therapeutic areas and stages of development" — clinical development, validation, and commercial-supply preparation, all aligned to individual regulatory and filing timetables. The three major capex programmes are "nearing completion and validations are going on." Divi's sits inside the innovator's CMC filing ("I'm a part of the innovator CMC filing"), which is both the moat and the bottleneck. Kiran on inspection readiness: "We are completely ready for all regulatory submissions. We are ready for inspection anytime."
- **Peptides / GLP-1.** Strategic investment area. Customer programmes progressing "across multiple phases"; qualification and validation of **several peptide fragments** expected to advance "over the coming quarters." Several fragments are already "being validated, supplied," with more in line. Capacity expanding in **both solid-phase and liquid-phase** synthesis, plus **multiple additional 3,000-litre SPPS** units "because we see a lot of future opportunity." Management would not confirm whether any GLP-1 commercial supply occurred this quarter. The differentiator is the depth of backward integration — see §6a.
- **Nutraceuticals.** ₹298 cr (+19% YoY, +24% QoQ off ₹240 cr). Twentieth year in the segment: from 2 products at inception to **100+ offerings** across human health, animal health and dietary supplements in multiple forms. "Actively expanding in both capabilities and capacities."
- **Contrast media.** *Iodine* — commercial, and the most concrete good news on the call: multi-year contracts with two customers being signed, one already commercialised, the second starting within months, "substantial quantities going forward." *Gadolinium* — **walked back**: still at qualification (Phase II/III), and Kiran corrected the record unprompted — "That's what I said last time. I didn't say that we did validations… Right now, the project is on slow phase with them on the Gadolinium side."
- **Unit 3 / Kakinada.** Now "assumes a large role within our production network," but *indirectly*: selected pre-chemistry operations for backward integration plus phased transfer of manufacturing off Units 1 and 2. Purpose is to free regulator-approved GMP capacity at the older units for higher-value work. Full regulatory qualification of Kakinada is the long-term plan but carries a hard lag — "**even after you validate a certain new project, FDA will take its own time, 1 or 2 years since it's a new place.**" In the meantime, "we are filling the plant with pre-chemistry products."
- **Technology / process.** Continuous flow chemistry, biocatalysis and advanced automation progressing across the network; process intensification on selected products; green chemistry and energy efficiency framed as long-term operational strategy rather than a project.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Full backward integration in peptides — evidenced, not asserted.** "We are the only ones who start from basic raw materials, build our own peptide building blocks… Then we have protected amino acid. We do dipeptide, tripeptides. We have gone into fragments." And on the manufacturing chain: "We do our own resins. We manufacture our own FMOC, BOC-protected amino acids, tags." Kiran was explicit that the ambition is **"the largest integrated player"** — a deliberate re-framing away from a pure scale race.
- **In-house KSMs and intermediates in generics.** Named as the reason the generic book held up through the solvent shock: "our ability to manufacture certain key starting materials and intermediates in-house which continues to strengthen our supply assurance and operational efficiency." The 31.2% net material consumption is the numeric evidence.
- **Embedded in the innovator's CMC filing.** "I'm a part of the innovator CMC filing… it goes into their filings." Once Divi's is written into a regulatory submission, displacing it requires the customer to refile — the switching cost is regulatory, not commercial.
- **Non-compete with customers.** "We do not compete with our customers. We are actually playing a complementary role. That's why our customers like us." No formulations arm — the structural argument against forward-integrated CDMO rivals.
- **Thirty-year track record as a selection criterion.** "We are close to, I would say, 30-year-old company who has been in CDMO. We are one of the first CDMOs in India." Asked whether the wave of new Indian CDMO entrants would compress pricing, Kiran's answer was that price is not the deciding variable: innovators "look at sustainability, they look at safety issues, they look at your EHS capabilities, your effluent management system, your employee health care system."
- **Supply reliability as a demonstrated, not claimed, asset.** "We never had a production loss or a shipment stoppage in the last few months" — through a quarter of port congestion, blank sailings and solvent scarcity.

business.body: Divi's Laboratories Limited manufactures and supplies high-quality Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and intermediates to global innovator pharmaceutical companies, and is a trusted partner to 12 of the top 20 global pharmaceutical companies. latest_quarter.body:
Gross margin printed ~68.8% (net material consumption 31.2%), well above the ~60% FY26 level — and management spent most of the Q&A talking it back down. Three forces are tangled together:

1. **Mix.** CS at 60% vs 55% last quarter is inherently richer. Nilima: "Considering this quarter, we did have more of custom synthesis, which is 60%. We do see the margins slightly higher than the previous quarter."
2. **Inventory capitalisation.** The ~₹500 cr change in inventory (vs ₹50–100 cr normal) mechanically lifts reported gross profit. Nilima's stated causes: the 3-month rolling buffer, and validation-batch production converting into WIP/intermediates/finished goods. She also made the compounding point plainly — "when there is an increase in the price of the raw materials, the cost of your intermediates and your work in progress and your finished goods also would go up substantially." That is inflation being carried onto the balance sheet at cost, which will flow through COGS later.
3. **FX.** An analyst attributed the margin surprise directly to INR depreciation and management did not push back — though the below-the-line forex line was a ₹7 cr *loss*.

Against these, the genuine headwind is **solvents**: "solvents have become almost double or triple the price. Certain solvent-based raw materials have increased substantially because of the issue in the Middle East." Nilima: "Mainly we saw it on the solvent side, **which we never saw before**." Divi's has pushed some of it through — "even we have increased our price slightly wherever possible with our customers because otherwise the products become unviable to even produce" — and continues to "evaluate commercially appropriate mechanisms" with customers, but the pass-through lags and was refused any quantification ("we manufacture close to 60 products now. I cannot generalize"). A striking scale marker on solvent intensity: **"If you take a peptide, it's almost like use about 2,000 litres per 1 kilo."**

Management's own framing is that quarterly margin is not the right unit of analysis — "let's not look at it on an individual quarter basis. Rather, we look at it on a year basis, where sometimes there's a lumpiness." The year-level answer they gave is ~60% gross and flat EBITDA.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Consolidated total income ₹3,144 cr (+24.3% YoY) but **constant-currency standalone growth only 10%**; PAT ₹902 cr (+65.5%); PBT ₹1,180 cr (+61%). Mix moved **55/45 → 60/40 in favour of Custom Synthesis**, driven partly by validation-batch shipments from the dedicated capex. Gross margin printed ~68.8% (NMC 31.2%) but was flattered by a **₹500 cr inventory change** vs a ₹50–100 cr norm; management guided FY27 gross back to **~60%** with EBITDA "similar as last year," and did not dispute IIFL's adjusted 55–58% GM / 28–30% EBITDA. Forex swung to a ₹7 cr **loss** (from a ₹39 cr gain). Nutraceuticals ₹298 cr (+19% YoY, +24% QoQ), 20-year milestone, 100+ products. **Three dedicated CS projects (~₹2,000 cr, ~70% capitalised) completed validation and shipped material to customers** — commercial start now gated purely on innovator filings and agency clearance. Peptides: several more **3,000-litre SPPS** units being installed; backward integration re-framed as the goal ("largest *integrated* player"). Generics: 4 DMFs, **Brivaracetam and Ticagrelor**, commercial volumes in **3–6 months**, one exclusivity in negotiation. Contrast media: **Iodine multi-year contracts with 2 customers — one commercialised, second within months**; **Gadolinium explicitly walked back to Phase II/III qualification, "on slow phase."** Kakinada now absorbing pre-chemistry to free GMP space at Units 1/2; full FDA qualification a **1–2 year** wait. Utilisation **80–85% across all three units**. Cash ₹3,611 cr (from ₹3,414 cr), CWIP ₹2,034 cr (from ₹2,113 cr), ₹451 cr capitalised. Q4 FY26's ₹74 cr Labour Code one-off did not recur. Guidance unchanged and **not raised**: double-digit FY27 growth.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did the ~₹500 cr inventory change normalise, and did gross margin fall toward the guided ~60% as management implied; (2) did Brivaracetam/Ticagrelor commercial volumes actually move within the 3–6 month window; (3) did the **second** iodine contrast-media customer commercialise "in the next few months" and were the two multi-year contracts signed; (4) any innovator filing/agency clearance converting the three dedicated projects to commercial supply, and did CS mix hold at 60% or revert toward 50/50; (5) constant-currency growth vs reported — is the underlying still ~10%; (6) Gadolinium — still "slow phase" or did the customer advance to Phase III; (7) has solvent pricing normalised, and if so did the promised inventory-value/volume unwind hit margins; (8) utilisation above 85% and any Kakinada regulatory milestone; (9) CWIP and the remaining ~30% of the ₹2,000 cr programme; (10) first dividend/buyback commentary — cash now ₹3,611 cr with no leverage._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** **Double-digit, FY27 — restated three times by two speakers.** Kiran: "I would like to stick to my statement saying that we will show double-digit growth no matter what"; and again "we would assure a double-digit growth for sure." Nilima: "if you want to look at a revenue projection, we are looking at double-digit growth." Asked explicitly whether Q1's strength implied *upside* to the ~10% dollar-revenue growth given at Q4, Kiran declined to raise the number.
- **Gross margin:** **~60% for the full year** — "At gross level, I would say it was approximately 60% all over the year." Q1's ~68% is explicitly disowned as a run-rate: "there would be lumpiness. Next quarter could be lower or higher."
- **EBITDA margin:** **"similar as last year"** (i.e. flat vs FY26) — no expansion guided despite the Q1 print.
- **Mix:** deliberately unguided. Kiran wants "a healthy mix always"; if regulatory approvals arrive faster "the ratio will be higher in terms of CS because commercial volumes will start moving."
- **Generics — dated:** 4 DMFs filed, validation quantities supplied, customers qualifying now. Named molecules **Brivaracetam** and **Ticagrelor**. "**We are expecting in the next 3 to 6 months, only commercial volumes will move out.**" One customer is negotiating a **long-term exclusivity** arrangement.
- **Contrast media — dated:** Iodine-based — long-term **multi-year contracts being signed with 2 customers**; commercialisation for one **already started**, the second **"we will start in the next few months"**, and "this will be substantial quantities going forward."
- **Capex / commissioning:** three major dedicated CS projects ~**₹2,000 cr** total, **~70% capitalised**, validations **completed**, commercial supply gated on innovator filing + agency approval. Peptides — **acquiring/installing several additional 3,000-litre SPPS** reactors.
- **Utilisation:** **80–85% across all three units** (Nilima declined to break it out unit-by-unit).
- **Inventory policy:** 3-month rolling stocking continues for as long as Middle East uncertainty persists — a decision taken "around March."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
There is no disclosed order book — the CDA wall is absolute this quarter and management said so repeatedly ("I wish to share more, but I'm bound by CDAs not to share"). What *was* quantified:

- **~18–20 Custom Synthesis projects are commercialised or being commercialised** as we speak, alongside "several projects in the pipeline."
- The **three dedicated-capex projects are three completely different products** (Kiran confirmed this explicitly when pressed on whether the fragments served the same molecule) — so the ₹2,000 cr is spread across three independent approval paths, not concentrated in one.
- **Validation-batch revenue is already in the P&L.** Asked whether the CS uptick contained any dedicated-capex contribution, Kiran did not deny it: "we are undergoing validation of some of the capex projects. So a certain amount of product has also been shipped to the customer."
- **Further validation batches will recur through FY27** — "we do have several projects which are coming up in the next quarters, which will require validations," many of which "may not require large investments" because existing facilities can absorb them.
- Management refused every attempt to size it: no phase-wise project split, no validation-to-commercial multiplier ("Some products, the annual demand is not more than 1,000 kgs. Some products we manufacture are 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes"), no top-five product growth, no capacity figure.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Peptide fragments as the primary growth engine.** "We have seen amazing opportunities in the fragment segment and several opportunities… a lot of them are in pipeline. Some of them are in clinical phases. Some are going through validations right now." The 3,000-litre SPPS additions are the capital vote behind that statement.
- **Three dedicated CS assets awaiting the starting gun.** ₹2,000 cr, validations done, three distinct molecules. If agencies move fast, "the ratio will be higher in terms of CS because commercial volumes will start moving" — the single largest swing factor in the FY27–28 P&L.
- **Iodine contrast media contracts.** Two multi-year customer contracts converting from qualification to commercial within the year — the only optionality on this call with a dated, near-term commercial trigger.
- **Generic post-patent-expiry pipeline.** 4 DMFs, Brivaracetam/Ticagrelor, commercial in 3–6 months, plus a potential long-term exclusivity — small individually but it addresses the flat-generics problem.
- **Kakinada as a capacity-arbitrage asset.** Even unqualified, Unit 3 releases GMP space at Units 1/2 for higher-value finished API — the return arrives as mix, not as Unit-3 revenue.
- **Nutraceuticals capacity expansion** into "a rapidly evolving global market" — 20-year-old business now compounding at ~20%.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Remain deliberately API-led - concentrating on generic APIs, custom synthesis and nutraceutical ingredients so as not to compete with customers and to deepen expertise in the chemistries that matter
- Advance backward integration, with Unit 3 at Kakinada producing starting materials and intermediates in-house while releasing GMP capacity at existing units for new products and customer requirements
- Treat integration as a mindset beyond in-house key starting materials - controlling quality, managing impurities and safeguarding supply to strengthen compliance, reduce variability and improve cost efficiency
- Build Custom Synthesis as the central long-term growth engine, taking innovator programmes through development, validation and commercial manufacturing of complex APIs and intermediates
- Strengthen peptide capabilities across chemistry, manufacturing and technology platforms through the Peptide Centre of Excellence and a backward-integrated model covering complex building blocks and fragments
- Grow the Nutraceuticals portfolio on the breadth of carotenoids and value-added ingredients, with continued capacity strengthening
- Maintain a diversified sourcing model with a steadily expanding domestic supplier base and prudent inventory buffers to reinforce supply resilience
- Deepen the scientific and technological platform through greater automation and expansion of advanced flow chemistry capabilities to execute increasingly complex chemistries at scale
- Engineering-led scale: plants designed to run volumes from kilos to thousands of metric tonnes with the same consistency, giving predictable supply and fast response to demand shifts
- Advance green chemistry practices by improving atom efficiency, reducing waste and enhancing solvent recovery and reuse
- Sustain quality and compliance credentials as a differentiator, backed by approvals from USFDA, EU GMP agencies, Health Canada, TGA, ANVISA, COFEPRIS, PMDA and MFDS and a team of about 2,800 QA and QC professionals
- Keep capital allocation disciplined - fund a large investment programme while maintaining a robust liquidity position and a healthy balance sheet
- Dividends are recommended by the Board under the Company's Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy, published on the Company's website pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, and are subject to Member approval at the AGM. Unclaimed dividend lying in the Unpaid Dividend Account for seven consecutive years, together with the underlying shares, is transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund as required by Section 124(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, with periodic reminders and newspaper notices sent to shareholders beforehand; eligible unclaimed dividends up to FY 2017-18 have been transferred. Remuneration of Executive Directors is set under a Nomination and Remuneration Policy and comprises a fixed component plus a variable component linked to the net profits of the Company, with a five-year tenure for the Managing Director and Whole-time Directors, three months' notice for termination and no provision for severance fees. Foreign exchange and other financial risks are managed through the Company's framework for identification, monitoring and mitigation of various risks, and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year.
- SBTi approval obtained for both near-term and net-zero greenhouse gas targets
- GHG footprint verified annually by an external agency as per ISO 14064-1
- Carbon Footprint of a Product (CFP) assessment for two selected products verified by an external agency in line with ISO 14067:2018
- Reducing dependency on fossil fuel sources and focusing on renewable sources for power and heat energy
- ISO 14001 Environment Management System certification maintained
- Solvent recovery and reuse plus green chemistry implementation to reduce waste generation; recycle-and-reuse programmes strengthened; solid waste handled per MoEFCC and Pollution Control Board regulations
- Reasonable assurance obtained on the 9 BRSR-Core indicators (GHG, water, energy, waste, employee wellbeing and safety, gender diversity, inclusive development, customer and supplier fairness, business openness) from Bureau Veritas (India) Private Limited
- Health and safety management systems aligned with the Factories Act, Explosives Act and applicable international ISO standards, reviewed and audited periodically with incident-driven corrective and preventive action
- Policies covering NGRBC Principles P1-P9 (except P7) approved by the Board or authorised Executive Director, including a Code of Ethics and Business Conduct, Whistle Blower Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct and Sustainable Procurement Policy, Labour and Human Rights Policy, CSR Policy, EHS and Environmental Sustainability Policy, and Information Security Policies
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company continues to make steady progress on its capital expenditure programmes. The Kakinada (Unit 3) project, an Export-Oriented Unit operational since January 2025, is being scaled up in phases; it supports backward integration through production of select starting materials and intermediates while enabling release of GMP capacity at existing units. In addition, capital expenditure programmes at Unit 1 (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Telangana) and Unit 2 (Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh) are progressing across various stages of implementation and regulatory approvals; these projects, backed by long-term business commitments, are focused on capacity expansion and enhancement of capabilities in complex chemistries. Management reports no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the year-end and the date of the report, and no change in the nature of business of the Company or its subsidiaries.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Generics remained steady despite persistent pricing pressure: value growth was moderated by pricing conditions while volumes across the core portfolio were stable, with no loss of customers or market share
- Custom Synthesis was the key growth driver during the year, with rising contribution to overall revenues and a healthy pipeline across development, validation and commercial stages
- Nutraceuticals delivered healthy performance on steady demand recovery and established capabilities in carotenoids and other value-added ingredients
- Multiple Custom Synthesis programmes are expected to move towards commercial manufacturing over the next 12 to 24 months, subject to regulatory approvals
- A balanced portfolio spanning patent-phase opportunities to late lifecycle programmes reduces concentration risk and supports a steady growth trajectory
- Partners are increasingly selective in choosing CDMO providers, favouring long-standing relationships with global innovators and a proven record in EHS, sustainability and compliance
- Near-term challenge flagged: potential impact of geopolitical uncertainty and policy changes on input costs and supply conditions, met with disciplined risk management and close supply-chain coordination
- Industry backdrop of value shifting toward innovation-led and specialty therapies, with growth becoming highly selective and favouring players combining scientific differentiation with disciplined execution
- Rising compliance thresholds across major markets are expected to consolidate participation toward chemistry-strong, regulatory-reliable suppliers, favouring established manufacturers
- Capacity bottlenecks in high-barrier segments such as peptides, HPAPIs and containment-intensive chemistries create advantages for differentiated suppliers
- Peptide-linked demand supported by the rise of GLP-1 therapies and a peptide therapeutics market estimated at ~USD 140 billion in 2025 projected to reach ~USD 295 billion by 2033
- Process efficiencies and cost discipline protected the generics franchise through the pricing cycle
- Healthy pipeline of Custom Synthesis projects across development, validation and commercial stages
- Steady flow of RFPs, site visits and progress on multiple programmes with global innovators
- Three major capex-backed projects linked to long-term supply commitments
- A few Custom Synthesis projects moving closer to commercial volumes
- Active engagement with global pharmaceutical companies across multiple clinical phases in peptides, supported by the Peptide Centre of Excellence
- As products evolve from patent-phase opportunities to late lifecycle programmes, new molecules continue to enter the pipeline
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A headline blow-out — consolidated income +24% and PAT +66% — that shrinks sharply once you strip the two things management itself flagged: constant-currency standalone revenue grew only **10%**, and the 68.8% gross margin was flattered by a **₹500 cr inventory change** against a ₹50–100 cr normal run-rate. The real operating news is that the three dedicated Custom Synthesis capex projects (~₹2,000 cr, ~70% capitalised) have **completed validation and shipped material to customers**, moving the story from "will it get built" to "when will the innovator's agency approve it" — a gate entirely outside Divi's control. Management's only hard commitment is double-digit FY27 growth, and Nilima explicitly guided full-year gross margin back to **~60%** with EBITDA margin "similar as last year" — an implicit admission that Q1's print does not hold.
